_comment: More voice for the HEMS missions (second set of conversations): the objective read by the dispatcher for each kind of mission, the crew briefing for transfers, organ transport and search and rescue, updates during the ground operations, the reaction to a death and to a hard landing, the call to the hospital and its answer, the marshal notice and the chats during the flight. No LVAR: the mission calls them with speak <say:KEY> (macros voice objective, voice briefing chat, voice ground update, voice patient died, voice hospital approach, voice marshal notice, voice cruise chat). The lines of a conversation with the same group are written so that option k of each belongs together (coherent variety). Written in a colloquial but professional tone, without warning prefixes.

messages.trigger: the dispatcher reads the objective of an accident mission
o: Get to the scene, assess the patient and keep us updated. If they need a hospital, take them to the nearest one.
Your task: reach the site, give first care and tell us what you find. Transport to a nearby hospital if needed.
Head for the location, take care of the patient and update us. Bring them to a hospital if necessary.
Reach the site and assess the situation. Treat the patient and, if needed, transport them to the closest hospital.

messages.trigger: objective of a search and rescue mission
o: Fly to the last known position and start the search. When you find the person, rescue them and take them to a hospital.
We need you to search the area around the last known position. Recover the person and bring them to hospital.
Start the search from the last reported position. Find the person, rescue them and deliver them to a nearby hospital.
Go to the last known position and begin the search. Rescue whoever you find and transport them to hospital.

messages.trigger: objective of the overdue vehicle search
o: Start from the last known position and follow the probable route of the vehicle. Find the driver, rescue them and take them to hospital.
Search along the route the vehicle most likely took. When you find the driver, rescue them and transport them to hospital.
Fly the probable route from the last known position and look for the vehicle. Find and rescue the driver, then hospital.
We lost contact on that route. Follow it, find the vehicle and the driver, and bring them to a hospital.

messages.trigger: objective of the parked car search
o: The vehicle was found parked: fly there and search the area around it. Find the owner, rescue them and take them to hospital.
Go to the parked vehicle and search around it. When you find the owner, recover them and bring them to hospital.
Start at the parked car and widen the search. Find and rescue the owner, then transport them to a hospital.
The car is there but its owner is missing. Search around it and take the owner to hospital once found.

messages.trigger: objective of the search around a house
o: Fly to the house and search the area around it. Find the missing person, rescue them and take them to hospital.
Start at the house and search the surroundings. When you find the person, recover them and transport them to hospital.
The person left the house on foot. Search around it, find them and bring them to a hospital.
Go to the house, search the surrounding area, rescue the person and deliver them to a nearby hospital.

messages.trigger: objective of a patient transfer
o: Pick up the patient at the designated point and transfer them safely to the destination. A smooth flight is the priority.
This is a transfer: load the patient at the indicated point and take them to the destination, safe and comfortable.
Collect the patient at the designated point and fly them to the destination. Keep the ride smooth.
Your task: take over the patient at the pickup point and transfer them safely to the receiving hospital.

messages.trigger: objective of an organ transport
o: Collect the organ at the designated point and bring it to the destination within the time limit. Every minute counts.
Organ transport: pick it up at the indicated point and deliver it on time. The clock is already running.
Pick up the organ at the designated point and fly it to the destination before the time limit. Be quick and careful.
Your task: collect the organ and deliver it to the destination in time. The receiving team is waiting.

messages.trigger: objective of an injured only mission
o: Choose your landing point, rescue the casualty and take them to the destination you prefer.
Reach the casualty, pick the landing point you like and bring them to the hospital of your choice.
Rescue the casualty where they are and transport them to the destination of your choice.
Go to the casualty, take care of them and transfer them to the destination you prefer.
Transfer mission. We collect the patient at the designated point and take them to the destination. Let's plan it carefully.
This is a patient transfer. Pickup at the sending point, then straight to the receiving hospital.
Transfer flight, crew. We load the patient and fly them to the destination as smoothly as possible.
Transfer today. The priority is a smooth ride for the patient.
Copy. I set the route to the pickup first, then the destination, and check the weather on both.
Understood. Two legs: pickup and destination. I prepare the navigation and the radio calls.
Copilot copy. The route to the pickup is set and the destination follows once the patient is aboard.
Got it. I handle the navigation and I will call the receiving hospital in advance.
Doc copy. I take the handover at the pickup, check the monitoring and the drips, and make sure the patient is stable for the flight.
Doc here. Handover first, then I check the lines and the monitors before we lift.
Copy. I will review the patient with the sending team and keep an eye on them in flight.
Understood. Handover, stabilisation, then transport.
Rear crew copy. Stretcher and monitoring are ready for loading.
Chief copy. The cabin is clear and the stretcher is prepared.
Rear crew ready. We help with the loading and secure everything for flight.
Copy. Stretcher, straps and equipment are ready. We load without hurry.
Good. Safe transfer, crew. We lift when the checklists are done.
Thank you all. Let's do this one properly.
Perfect. Smooth and safe, as always.
Alright, let's go and bring the patient across.
Organ transport. Time is critical: we collect the organ and deliver it within the time limit.
This is an organ run, crew. The clock is ticking, so we keep everything tight.
Organ transport. Pickup, then the shortest safe route to the destination.
We have an organ to deliver on time. Quick and clean, please.
Copy. I plan the fastest route and watch the clock. The destination will be informed.
Understood. I set the route and I will tell you the time left at every stage.
Copilot copy. Direct routing to the pickup, then to the destination, no detours.
Got it. I handle the navigation and the calls to the receiving hospital.
Doc copy. At pickup I check the container: seal, temperature and documents.
Doc here. I verify the paperwork and the container before we leave.
Copy. I take care of the container and the documentation.
Understood. Container, seal and paperwork checked at the pickup.
Rear crew copy. The container travels in the cabin and we secure it for flight.
Chief copy. We secure the container and keep the cabin clear.
Rear crew ready. The container is strapped in before we lift.
Copy. We handle the container with care and keep it safe in the cabin.
Good. Let's go, and let's be on time.
Thanks, crew. Fast and safe.
Alright. Every minute counts, let's move.
Perfect. We lift as soon as we are ready.
Search and rescue. We start from the last known position and cover the area systematically. Everybody looks outside.
This is a search mission, crew. We search in a pattern and everyone keeps their eyes out.
Search and rescue today. We take it step by step from the last known position.
SAR mission. We search carefully and call out everything we see.
Copy. I set the search area and the limits and I call what I see on my side.
Understood. I prepare the search pattern and I watch the terrain.
Copilot copy. Navigation is mine and I help with the search on the right.
Got it. I handle the area map and the radio.
Doc copy. When we find the person I assess and stabilise. Hoist or ground depends on the site.
Doc here. I will be ready as soon as we find them.
Copy. First we find them, then I take care of the assessment.
Understood. Medical kit ready, hoist or ground as the site allows.
Rear crew copy. Hoist gear and ground kit are ready, and I watch the left side.
Chief copy. The gear is ready for hoist or ground operations.
Rear crew ready. We are set for whatever the terrain needs.
Copy. I keep my eyes on the left side and the equipment ready.
Good. Eyes open, and call everything you see.
Thanks. Let's find them.
Alright, crew. Let's start the search.
Perfect. We lift when ready, and everybody watches.
Doc, how are we doing down there?
Chief, can you give me a status?
How is the patient, Doc?
Any update from the ground, Chief?

messages.trigger: stage crew deployment
o: The crew is moving to the patient and the equipment is on the way.
We are deploying now. The team is reaching the patient.
The crew is on the way to the patient with the equipment.
We are setting up on the spot, the crew is already moving.

messages.trigger: stage assessment and treatment, patient stable
o: The patient is stable. Assessment and treatment are ongoing.
Stable for now. We are continuing the assessment and treatment.
The patient is holding well. We are still treating.
Vitals are steady. Treatment is in progress.

messages.trigger: stage assessment and treatment, patient serious
o: The patient is in a serious condition. We are treating and keeping a close eye on the vitals.
Serious condition. Treatment is ongoing and we monitor closely.
The patient is not good. We are working on stabilising.
Vitals are unstable. We are still treating.

messages.trigger: stage assessment and treatment, patient critical
o: The patient is critical. We are doing everything we can, please stand by.
Critical condition. We are working fast, stay with us.
The patient is critical. Treatment is ongoing and we will tell you as soon as we can move.
Very unstable. We are treating right now.

messages.trigger: stage CPR
o: CPR in progress. We continue the resuscitation.
We are resuscitating. CPR is ongoing.
Resuscitation in progress. We will update you.
CPR is ongoing. We do not stop.

messages.trigger: stage patient loading
o: The patient is packaged and we are loading.
Loading the patient now, the crew is coming back.
We are bringing the patient to the helicopter.
The stretcher is on the move. We load next.

messages.trigger: stage final crew return
o: The crew is back at the helicopter. We will be ready in a moment.
Everyone is returning to the helicopter, almost done.
Final checks, then we close up.
The team is back aboard, we are nearly set.

messages.trigger: who transports: the helicopter
o: We take the patient with the helicopter.
The helicopter will transport the patient.
The patient flies with us.
We will carry the patient aboard.

messages.trigger: who transports: the ambulance
o: The ambulance will take the patient to the hospital and we give them the handover.
The ambulance transports and we hand the patient over to them.
The patient goes by ambulance. We give the crew the handover.
The ambulance team takes the patient from here.

messages.trigger: remaining ground time, {0} minutes
o: About {0} minutes before we are ready.
We need about {0} more minutes.
Roughly {0} minutes to go.
Give us about {0} minutes.

messages.trigger: remaining ground time, one minute
o: About a minute left.
One more minute and we are ready.
Roughly a minute to go.
Give us a minute.

messages.trigger: remaining ground time, almost done
o: We are almost ready, any moment now.
Nearly done, standby for departure.
Just a few seconds more.
Almost there, we call you when ready.
Copy, thanks.
Understood. We stay ready.
Good. We are here.
Copy. Call me when you are ready.

messages.trigger: a patient dies of the clinical conditions
o: Doc here. No pulse and no breathing. I am sorry, we lost the patient.
We lost the patient. I record the time of death.
The patient has died. There is nothing more we can do.
No vital signs. I am sorry, the patient is gone.
Copy, Doc. Thank you for everything you did.
Understood. Take the time you need.
I am sorry, Doc. We stay at your disposal.
Copy. Let me know when we can move.

messages.trigger: a patient dies of the impact of a hard landing
o: That was a very hard impact! Doc, how is the patient?
Doc, check the patient, that landing was too hard!
Doc, are you okay? How is the patient after that touchdown?
That impact was bad! Doc, patient status?
I am sorry. The impact was too much, the patient has died.
No pulse. The impact was fatal, we lost the patient.
We lost the patient. The hard landing was too much for them.
The patient did not survive the impact. I am sorry.
Understood. I am sorry, crew.
Copy. That was on me. Doc, take your time.
I hear you, Doc. I am sorry.
Copy. We take it from here.

messages.trigger: after a hard landing
o: Everybody okay? Report!
Crew, status report!
All right, everyone report!
Report, everybody!
I am okay, but that was very hard.
Copilot okay. Let's check the helicopter.
I am fine. That touchdown was hard.
Okay up front, but we must inspect the aircraft.
Doc okay. I check the patient right now.
I am fine. Checking the patient.
Doc here, all right. I am looking after the patient.
I am okay, let me check the patient first.

messages.trigger: the copilot calls the hospital with a patient aboard; {0}: minutes to go
o: Hospital, HEMS helicopter is inbound with one patient, ETA about {0} minutes.
Hospital, HEMS inbound with a patient on board, about {0} minutes out.
Hospital, we are the HEMS helicopter with one patient, ETA {0} minutes.
Hospital, HEMS is inbound, one patient aboard, expect us in about {0} minutes.

messages.trigger: the copilot calls the hospital with an organ aboard
o: Hospital, HEMS helicopter inbound with the organ, ETA about {0} minutes.
Hospital, we bring the organ, about {0} minutes out. Please have the team ready.
Hospital, HEMS is inbound with the organ, ETA {0} minutes.
Hospital, organ on board, we will be with you in about {0} minutes.

messages.trigger: the copilot calls the hospital with a deceased patient aboard
o: Hospital, HEMS helicopter inbound, ETA about {0} minutes. The patient died during the mission.
Hospital, HEMS inbound in about {0} minutes. We have a deceased patient on board.
Hospital, HEMS helicopter, ETA {0} minutes, patient deceased in flight.
Hospital, we arrive in about {0} minutes. The patient did not survive.
HEMS, copy. The helipad is clear and the team will be waiting for you.
Copy, HEMS. We expect you on the helipad.
HEMS, understood. The helipad is ready and we will be there.
Copy. We wait for you on the helipad.
HEMS, copy. The transplant team is ready and waiting at the helipad.
Copy, HEMS. We are ready to receive the organ at the helipad.
HEMS, understood. The team will be at the helipad when you land.
Copy. The surgical team is ready for you.
HEMS, copy. We are sorry. We will wait for you at the helipad.
Copy, HEMS. Understood, we will be at the helipad.
HEMS, copy. We expect you on the helipad.
Copy. The team will receive you on the helipad.

messages.trigger: the hospital team receives the patient
o: Welcome. The trauma team is ready. What do we have?
Good to see you. We take over from here, what is the status?
Welcome. The team is ready, tell us about the patient.
We have the stretcher ready. Please give us the handover.
Doc here. Handover: the patient is stable, treated and monitored. All yours.
Here is the handover: the patient is treated and monitored, the details are in the report.
Patient treated and monitored, the whole report goes with you. They are in good hands.
Handover done. Everything we did is on the report, thank you for taking them.
Thank you, we take it from here. Good work.
Thanks, the patient is in our hands now.
Perfect, thank you. Have a safe flight back.
We have the patient. Thank you for the quick transport.

messages.trigger: the hospital receives the organ
o: We have the organ. Thank you, the team will take it from here.
Received. Thank you for bringing it on time.
The organ is ours now. Excellent work, crew.
Thanks, the surgical team is waiting. Great job.

messages.trigger: marshal present at the hospital, said some time before the arrival
o: Be informed that a marshal will guide you in at the hospital helipad.
The hospital has a marshal at the helipad to guide you in.
A marshal will be waiting for you at the helipad.
The hospital helipad has a marshal who will guide you.

messages.trigger: marshal present on the scene
o: A marshal will be on the scene to guide you in.
On scene there is a marshal who will direct your landing.
Be informed that a marshal is on the scene and will guide you.
The scene has a marshal waiting for you.

messages.trigger: chat during the flight to the scene
o: Everything looks fine so far. How are the conditions on your side?
We have a good tailwind today. Nice for a change.
The air is quiet. Let's keep it that way.
Smooth flight so far. Let's hope the landing is as easy.
Good on my side. The weather ahead is clear.
Nothing to report. Fuel and engines are fine.
Looks good. I watch the traffic and the weather.
All normal. I keep an eye on the sky ahead.
I am preparing the kit. Let me know when we are close.
Doc here. I go through the equipment while we fly.
The kit is checked. Ready when you are.
Medical bag ready. I check the monitor again.

messages.trigger: chat during the flight to the hospital
o: Alright, we are on our way. Let's keep it smooth for the patient.
Good work back there. Now we deliver the patient.
On our way. A steady flight for the patient, please.
We are moving. Keep me posted on the patient.
Copy. I keep monitoring and I tell you if something changes.
Doc here. The patient is under my eyes.
Understood. I keep treating and tell you at once if anything changes.
Copy. I stay with the patient.
I take care of the navigation and call the hospital in time.
Navigation set. I will call the hospital when we are closer.
The hospital will be informed. I watch the route.
Copy. Route is set and I will advise the hospital.

messages.trigger: two nautical miles from the pickup point of a patient transfer
o: We are two miles from the pickup point. Let us land and take over the patient.
Pickup point in two miles. We land, load and go.
Two miles out from the sending hospital. Prepare for the handover.
Almost at the pickup point. Prepare for landing.
Doc ready. I take the handover and check the monitors right away.
Doc here. Handover first, then we load.
Ready for the handover. I check the lines before loading.
Copy. I take over the patient as soon as we land.
Rear crew ready for the loading, stretcher prepared.
Chief here. The stretcher is ready and the cabin is clear.
Rear crew set. We load as soon as the doc gives the go.
Copy. Stretcher and straps ready.
Good. Landing at the pickup point.
Thanks. Let us set it down gently.
Alright, landing now.
Perfect. A smooth touchdown, please.

messages.trigger: two nautical miles from the pickup point of an organ transport
o: Two miles to the organ pickup. Time is tight, let us be quick.
Pickup in two miles. We land, load and leave straight away.
Almost at the pickup point. Check the time, we must be efficient.
Organ pickup two miles ahead. Prepare for a quick landing.
Doc ready. I check the container and the paperwork at once.
Doc here. Seal, temperature, documents: I check them first.
Ready. I handle the container and the papers.
Copy. I verify the container as soon as we land.
Rear crew ready. The container goes straight into the cabin.
Chief here. We secure the container right after loading.
Rear crew set. Straps ready for the container.
Copy. We take the container and secure it.
Good. Landing, then straight to the destination.
Thanks. Fast and safe.
Alright, let us be quick on the ground.
Perfect. Down and up again as soon as we can.
